prompt:
Edit the supplied painted manuscript map to correct ONE REGIONAL GEOGRAPHIC PROBLEM: KADJETI IS AN INLAND ROCK FORTRESS, not a sea-cliff castle. The source image is the exact edit target. Keep the same accomplished tempera/gouache manuscript style, mineral pigments, dark blue sea, antique-gold illumination border, fine architecture and rocky/wooded landscapes.

PRESERVE the six other main settings (Arabia upper-left palace, wilderness cave upper-middle-left, Khataeti upper-middle-right mountain stronghold, India upper-right palace, Mulghazanzar lower-middle-left coastal city, Gulansharo lower-middle-right merchant port), their relative positions, silhouettes and identities. Keep the title field upper-left and their pale name fields usable. Keep the full rectangular border and full canvas. Keep the large lower sea, the ships, and the central bay between the western and eastern ports. Keep continuous northern land behind the bay so an overland journey between Arabia and India is plausible. Do not add an eighth realm or any new principal city.

CORRECTION IN THE LOWER-RIGHT REGION:
- Remove the immediate shoreline from the base and sides of Kadjeti's fortress. It must NOT stand over sea, a tidal inlet, an island, or a coastal cliff.
- Shift the existing recognizable three-gated fortress somewhat lower into the far lower-right hinterland: its main wall around 87% of canvas width and 72% down from the top. Retain the three distinct LAND gate openings, steep rock, tall towers and imposing character.
- Surround it on every side with a substantial continuous belt of DRY rocky uplands, rough valleys, wooded hills and mountain ridges. Show that this is a remote destination beyond Gulansharo's coastal realm. Land must continue between the rock base and the lower/right borders; no water should touch or immediately surround the castle's rock.
- Recede the lower-right coastline westward toward the merchant port and the central/lower sea. Preserve Gulansharo's harbor as a coastal city. Its eastern hinterland now extends toward Kadjeti through a winding dry valley and mountain pass.
- Provide a winding overland approach from the Gulansharo side into the rocky Kadjeti country. One dark tunnel/passage entrance through an approaching rock spur may be visible; a tunnel is an approach, not a ring around the fortress. The three fortress gates must open onto dry ground.
- The upper-right Indian palace and remote Kadjeti must feel separated by a wide rugged inland region and ridges, not as close sea neighbors across a narrow inlet. Do not draw a special direct India–Kadjeti road.
- Keep a naturally quiet parchment name field below the relocated fortress, around x87%, y90–93% down. No drawn banner or modern box.

No lettering, numbers, labels, symbols, route lines, arrows, dotted roads, folding lines, user-interface elements, or watermark. Precise Georgian text and audited routes will be added separately. Change only what is necessary in the eastern/lower-right terrain and Kadjeti placement; retain the identity and visual quality of the rest of this existing painting. Opaque landscape canvas, same approximate 1.41:1 aspect ratio.
